precepts.text: Judas Maccabeus comforted the people out of the law and the prophets, put them in mind of the battles they had won before, and when he had stirred up their minds gave them their charge, showing the falsehood of the heathen and their breach of oaths. His vision was of Onias the high priest, a virtuous and good man, reverend in conversation, gentle in condition, well spoken, exercised from a child in virtue, praying for the whole body of the Jews. Take this holy sword and wound the adversaries; the people were well comforted by his words and set to try the matter manfully. A leader knows the condition of the battle, comforts out of the scriptures, and reworks the minds of children who still think Esau is a princess.
precepts.point: A captain adds that we are compared to fine gold, which has to be mined, so do not be afraid of perfection or of being great. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people that has been robbed, raped, and murdered.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Sirach says “Let us now praise famous men” and names them as “Leaders of the people”, leaders, not one. Second Maccabees shows what those leaders do. Judas Maccabeus was preparing the men for war, and we are at war too, brothers: against sin and against our physical enemies, the children of Satan, Edom, Esau.

First a leader has to know the condition of the battle. “And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.” If the first time you hear there is a war going on is weeks after it started, you are sleep. If you are not comforting yourself, your children, your wife and your husband out of the law and the prophets, you are not ready for the famine the Lord said is coming, when your stomach touches your back and your kids are looking at you.

“And when he had stirred up their minds, he gave them their charge, shewing them therewithal the falsehood of the heathen, and the breach of oaths.” That is why the class keeps showing that Esau is the devil, lying and breaking every treaty and oath. If your daughter secretly wants to be Tinkerbell, or wears the Frozen wig because she thinks Esau is still a princess, she does not see his breach of oaths. As a mother and a father you have to rework her mind and put her in the mindset of our fathers. Keep the body, take the mind: that was the slave master’s method, and the leader’s work is to take back the mind.

“And this was his vision”: leaders are visionaries, and where there is no vision the people perish. Onias was “a virtuous and a good man”; virtue is moral excellence, and our moral compass is God’s commandments that make us shine like gold. He was “reverend in conversation”, eloquent in speech; “gentle in condition”, keeping his composure, not hot-headed; “well spoken also”; and “exercised from a child in all points of virtue.” Nobody wakes up leading people. We are born leaders, but we become that in time. And “holding up his hands prayed for the whole body of the Jews”: leaders serve and sacrifice themselves for the betterment of the people.

Jeremias gave Judas a sword of gold: “Take this holy sword, a gift from God, with the which thou shalt wound the adversaries.” Then “Thus being well comforted by the words of Judas”: not Judas’s own mindset but the words of God, which comfort a people with a spirit of fear on them and stir them up “to valour, and to encourage the hearts of the young men.” They determined “courageously to set upon them, and manfully to try the matter by conflict.” That is the result of a great leader.

That is why the nations destroy the leaders first, because the leaders are in many cases the lifeline of the people. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people that has been robbed, raped and murdered, and no nation on this planet needs great leaders more than ours.

precepts.text: They said one to another, let us restore the decayed estate of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary. Nobody did it alone; the Bishop went to the streets with a reader. You will go further and sacrifice more for someone else than for yourself, which is why selfish people only go so far.
precepts.point: A captain adds that we are compared to fine gold, which has to be mined, so do not be afraid of perfection or of being great. A leader is needed to bring comfort to a people that has been robbed, raped, and murdered.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Sirach praises the “Leaders of the people”, plural, and First Maccabees shows how they worked: “They said one to another, Let us restore the decayed fortune of our people, and let us fight for our people and the sanctuary.” They said it one to another. Nobody tried to do it by himself. When the Bishop went to the streets, he had a reader; that is why the scriptures say go two by two. The Bishop has said for years that this work is too big for one man.

We are in that decayed estate now. The mindset of 99% of our people is in a horrible state: our women thinking they can wear tights outside and nothing is wrong, grown men going outside in a crop top with the belly out, our young women on the dance teams. If that does not put you in a different state of mind, you are destroyed. That is the urgency you see in the brothers teaching loud in the streets, and that is why the Bishop and the deacons teach the way they teach.

Restoring the decayed estate of our people is what is happening at IUSC: our women in order, our men in order, our children in order.

“Let us fight for our people”, and for the sanctuary. You will go way further for somebody else than you will for yourself, and sacrifice way more for someone else than for yourself. That is why selfish people only go so far: they are satisfied at some point. A leader’s mind is on the whole people, like the leaders Sirach praises, who left a name behind them.

precepts.text: Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent in their instructions. You can tell a leader by his speech; everything the leaders here say they prove from scripture. Why are you there: because he talks about baby oil, or because he cannot break down Romans 3?
precepts.point: You cannot boast in sacrificing as though it makes you special, because it is done; Christ died for us. Justification is through Christ, and it is in the same chapter as let God be true and every man a liar.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
How do you identify a leader? Some people say you can’t say he’s not a leader. Yes, we can, because you can tell who a man is by his speech. Sirach gives the rubric: “Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions”.

Leaders of the people by their counsels: you should be able to tell by their godly counsel, coming from the Bible, whether or not they are leaders of the people. By their knowledge of learning meet for the people: Bishop just showed the works in Chronicles and the deeds in Nehemiah 13, proving what Romans 3 means. Wise and eloquent are their instructions.

The leaders here in Israel United in Christ prove everything they say with the scriptures. That is why I am here. Why are you there? What is your agenda? Are you there because he talks about baby oil? Are you there because he cannot break down Romans 3? The Bible is the rubric that lets us know who the real leaders are and who are not.

precepts.text: Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth when the flood came.
precepts.point: Without Noah none of us would be here; Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood.

note.label: Genesis 6: The Sons of God and the Preparing of the Ark

precepts.why:
Genesis says Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord, that he “was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Ecclesiasticus says the same of him: “Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant unto the earth, when the flood came.”

Without Noah none of us would be here. He was the remnant left unto the earth, and his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth repopulated the earth after the flood. “An everlasting covenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.”

precepts.text: Noah was found perfect and righteous and was left as a remnant unto the earth.
precepts.point: Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; Leviticus 18 opens those laws.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
Noah was still perfect and righteous after this. “Noah was found perfect and righteous; in the time of wrath he was taken in exchange for the world; therefore was he left as a remnant unto the earth, when the flood came. An everlasting covenant was made with him, that all flesh should perish no more by the flood.”

He drank too much and was uncovered within his tent, but one fall does not undo righteousness. He remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High.

precepts.text: The blessing of all men and the covenant rested on the head of Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob and divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

precepts.why:
“Abraham was a great father of many people: in glory was there none like unto him; Who kept the law of the most High, and was in covenant with him: he established the covenant in his flesh; and when he was proved, he was found faithful.” Therefore the Lord assured him by an oath “that he would bless the nations in his seed, and that he would multiply him as the dust of the earth, and exalt his seed as the stars.”

Then it shows where the promise went. “With Isaac did he establish likewise for Abraham his father’s sake the blessing of all men, and the covenant, And made it rest upon the head of Jacob.” He gave Jacob an heritage and divided his portions: “among the twelve tribes did he part them.”

So the father of many nations is not everybody. The blessing of all men and the covenant rest on the head of Jacob and are divided among the twelve tribes. Kings come out of that seed, including Christ, the King of kings.

precepts.text: The register of famous men opens the record in which Phinehas is honored.
precepts.point: These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, rose up from among the congregation with a javelin and thrust the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman through, and the plague was stayed. He is written in the register of famous men.

“Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.” This is the record in which Phinehas is honored, one of the fathers that begat us, praised for what he did in the sight of Moses and all the congregation.

precepts.text: We descend from the famous men of the book of the Lord.
precepts.point: Take pride in this: we are the descendants of the most famous men on the face of the earth. Our forefathers are mentioned in every single nation, and everybody wants to lay claim to them and to our book. That is why all nations hate us, and we will be famous again: the Most High will get Israel praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame, when he turns back our captivity before our eyes. Remember, Jerusalem is a people before it is a place.

note.label: Joshua 12: The Thirty and One Kings

precepts.why:
“Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.” Joshua was a mighty man: thirty and one kings he took down in the power of the Most High. We descend from the famous men of the book of the Lord.

Take pride in this: we are the descendants of the most famous men on the face of the earth. Our forefathers are mentioned in every single nation, and everybody wants to lay claim to them and to our book. That is why all nations hate us.

precepts.text: For Isaac's sake he made the blessing rest upon the head of Jacob, gave him an heritage, and divided his portions among the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: These are the curses we are under. Our heritage, the heathens, became our masters and our oppressors today. We are still under the curses of God, disconnected from our blessings and from our homeland.

note.label: Psalm 127: Except the Lord Build the House

precepts.why:
For Isaac’s sake, for Abraham his father’s sake, the Most High established the blessing and the covenant, and “made it rest upon the head of Jacob.” He acknowledged him in his blessing, “and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.”

That heritage divided among the twelve tribes is what we have been disconnected and discontinued from. Children are an heritage of the Lord, part of the portion given to Jacob, and we are still under the curses that cut us off from it.

precepts.text: The blessing of all men and the covenant made to rest upon the head of Jacob, and his inheritance divided among the twelve tribes.
precepts.point: The blessing that came down on all men is traced in the scripture to one head, and rested on Jacob and was divided among the twelve tribes.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
John came “to bear witness of the Light, that all men through him might believe.” He was not that Light; he prepared the way. That Light lights every man that comes into the world, and the blessing that came down on all men is traced in the scripture to one head: “With Isaac did he establish likewise for Abraham his father’s sake the blessing of all men, and the covenant, And made it rest upon the head of Jacob.”

“He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.” The blessing of all men and the covenant were made to rest upon the head of Jacob, and his inheritance was divided among the twelve tribes.
